name: TaskTales
synopsis: Awarded a Honourable Mention for the SUTD Infomation Systems Singtel Award. A gamified productivity app designed to incentivize good habits in task management, through engaging gameplay and an intuitive interface.
description:
TaskTales is a gamified productivity app designed to incentivize good habits in task management, through engaging gameplay and an intuitive interface. Users choose a class which best aligns to their personal goals, and can earn points by completing minor and major task quests, which are then used to defeat weekly bosses for cosmetic rewards.

The team was awarded a Honourable Mention for the SUTD Infomation Systems Singtel Award for their efforts.
process:
For this project, I worked on the concept design and UI/UX interface using Figma. My design process for TaskTales involved focusing on functionality over aesthetics, through the initial creation of a Lo-Fi Prototype. Here, I helped to lay out the necessary pages and user interactions, using game design principles to prioritise intuitive actions that made the main game mechanic simple to end users.

Once the team had established the app's purpose and goals, I then worked on a Hi-Fi Prototype with an accompanying mood board, to drive the art style of the application.

name: Ilumi-sync
synopsis: Awarded 3rd Place @ SBS Transit Hackathon 2025. A centralized MRT lighting system that detects light intensity along key entrances of the station, enabling real-time notifications for staff on which lights should be controlled from an intuitive dashboard.
description:
Ilumi-sync is a centralized MRT lighting system that detects light intensity along key entrances of the station, enabling real-time notifications for staff on which lights should be controlled from an intuitive dashboard. The main dashboard was built using React, taking data from a google spreadsheet populated by an ESP-32 and a LDR module.

The team was awarded 3rd Place at SBS Transit Hackathon 2025 and offered an internship position for their efforts.
process:
For this project, I took on the role of sole developer, while my partner worked on the hardware mechanics. We focused on creating a quality proof-of-concept, opting to create a workable prototype that showcased the real-time detection of light intensity from the ESP-32 and LDR Module, hence deciding on a simplified tech stack of a single page application and Google Sheets for data transmission.

I also focused on making the dashboard intuitive for MRT personnel who may not be trained in technology, ensuring only necessary information was displayed on the front with distinct colour changes to alert users when light intensity is too low at a location by first prototyping in Figma. This way, the dashboard would serve its main purpose of alerting staff even if they are preoccupied with other important duties, with the colour changes.

name: Blank Space
synopsis: Awarded 1st Place Advanced Team @ SUTD Mindsports Game Jam 2024. A space-themed point-and-click exploration game, where you play as a human researcher cataloguing certain species of interests across the universe, made using Godot.
description:
Blank Space is a space-themed point-and-click exploration game, where you play as a human researcher cataloguing certain species of interests across the universe. This was made during a one-week game jam for the theme 'Space', and creatively applies the theme in gameplay through the use of negative space, the 'space' key and the space art and story themes.

The team was awarded 1st Place Advanced Team at SUTD Mindsports Game Jam 2024 for their efforts.
process:
As the lead developer and primary coordinator for this project, I worked in a team of 2 artists and one other developer to deliver the basic gameplay by the deadline. We first worked together to develop the game concept, before splitting our tasks based on our roles and necessary features in order of priority.

The game itself was developed on Godot, the music was sourced from Freesound and the art was self-made. I worked on the procedural map generation scene, the journal data system and creature naming scene, using object oriented programming to simplify the procedure of adding each planet and corresponding creature to the game logic. My focus was based on creating a working gameplay loop to convey the game concept, hence the initial submission lacked some polish in terms of sound and uniqueness of gameplay.

The game was polished on completion of the game jam to its current state.

name: LepakLah!
synopsis: Awarded 3rd Place @ Dell InnovateFest 2024. An AI-powered activity management system for Active Aging Centres, bridging the gap between elderly and caregivers through a personalised buddy system, inclusive activity balloting and weekly activity voting.
description:
LepakLah! is an AI-powered activity management system for Active Aging Centres, bridging the gap between elderly and caregivers through a personalised buddy system, inclusive activity balloting and weekly activity voting. In partnership with Lion's Befrienders, this project aims to address the difficulties elderly residents face in attending activities at Active Aging Centres, as the current system depends on a first-come-first-serve application, causing elderly to be unable to guarantee attending with friends or being able to apply in time.

Under the mentorship of Dell, our team worked closely with the residents to create a product that was simple to use and effective in addressing the problem statement.The final product consisted of an elderly-facing mobile application, with user-centre design to guarantee ease of use, and a volunteer-facing web application to handle trend detection and AI activity generation.

The team was awarded 3rd Place at Dell InnovateFest 2024 for their efforts.
process:
The journey of developing LepakLah! was not an easy one, as it was my first experience using Flutter to develop the frontend of mobile applications. However, I sought to ensure I utilised good coding principles throughout the development phase, working on the design and development of an intuitive elderly-facing interface through initial prototyping n Figma.

Our design philosophy focused on the ease of use, through tap mechanics and increased use of images and icons to convey meaning. This design guided our development phase, and was validated by positive feedback from our user testing with elderly residents at Lions Befrienders Tampines Centre.

name: Lyf
synopsis: Made in partnership with Lyf One North Singapore. An AR camera application powered by Unity and Vuforia, which aims to increase engagement among residents by scanning specific colourful murals on the property and activating stickers, effects and virtual 3D models.
description:
Lyf is an AR camera application powered by Unity and Vuforia, which aims to increase engagement among residents on the property by scanning specific colourful murals on the property and activating an camera menu consisting of stickers, effects and virtual 3D models. The focus of the app was to increase mobility through these spaces, sparking conversations and shared memories through unique and self-made background for each image.

The application was made in partnership with Lyf One North Singapore, through a collaboration with Temasek Polytechnic. It was also showcased at multiple industry visits at Temasek Polytechnic.
process:
This application was a solo project and my first industry project. The idea and design of the application was conceived after an initial site visit, inspired by the vast array of unique art murals displayed across the property. My initial goal was to increase visibility of these art pieces, and through ideation I landed on photos as the chosen medium for preserving memories made near these murals.

As this was my first exploration with Vuforia, I focused on making the sticker menu appear reliably with the murals as image targets, before refocusing my efforts into expanding the library of assets available on the menu. The vast majority of assets were self-made, though some 3D models were sourced from Unity Asset Store in the interest of time and proof-of-concept.

name: iFlip
synopsis: Made during an internship @ Digital Dream Singapore. An interactive book projection connected to a Mixed Reality (MR) Room, detecting human interactions and page markers using computer vision to recreate immersive games and scenes in Unity.
description:
iFlip is an interactive book projection connected to a Mixed Reality (MR) Room, detecting human interactions and page markers on the book using computer vision to affect immersive games and scenes in the MR Room. The goal of the project was to tell immersive stories, where players could be transported into story scenes and interact with the story themselves.

This project was made during an internship at Digital Dream Singapore, and is property of Digital Dream Singapore.
process:
This project underwent multiple phases of proof-of-concepts, as I worked to develop a reliable image detection inside the MR room, eventually landing on the use of computer vision in Python for both image detection and gesture hand detection. Due to the difficulty of adjusting to different lightings based on the game content in unity, most of my efforts went into adjusting the values in Python to make the detection accurate.

The story chosen to display this technology was a twisted version of the little match girl, to explore how an immersive story medium can invoke deeper emotions in players. Each page of the story was tied to an interactive scene in the mixed reality room, putting the players in her position in this re-imagined classic tale.

The sound was sourced from Freesound, and the art for this project was made by me and in collaboration with another artist intern.

name: Befriender's Circle
synopsis: A feedback-driven web-based platform designed to support caregivers of all ages through 3D simulation training modules, voice-enabled AI chatbot for caregiving resources, and a caregiver community support forum.
description:
Befriender's Circle is a feedback-driven web-based platform designed to support caregivers of all ages, featuring 3D simulation training modules, voice-enabled AI chatbot for caregiving resources, and a caregiver community support forum. The goal of the application is to be a one-stop centre for all necessary information on caregiving, empowering individuals despite the difficulties faced in their caregiving journey.

The project was made in collaboration with Lion's Befrienders, through the Elements of Software Construction (ESC) module in SUTD.
process:
For this project, I took charge of the 3D training simulation feature, as well the UI/UX design of the application. We began the project by brainstorming the necessary features we wanted to develop, before dividing the workload amongst the team members. Through this ideation, we landed on three main features, each targeting different issues a caregiver might face in their journey.

The UI/UX was first prototyped on Figma, focusing on keeping interactions simple for all caregivers including elderly caregivers, and colour coding features for ease of identification. This design served as the baseline for other developers in the team to create their features with, though I worked on the final frontend version to coordinate all pages with the same design and margins.

For the training simulations, I created a training module on home safety based on research on reducing hazards at home, planning a series of questions and necessary assets. Using blender, I created a 3d model of a 2 room HDB apartment using 3D assets from Kaykits and some self-modelled assets for specific objects, with camera and object animation clips within the software. This scene was then rendered on the webpage using three.js, calling each clip in order of the planned questions a caregiver would be asked in the training module. At the end of the module, a score would be given based on the correct number of responses, and the module could be replayed anytime.

name: Whiskers
synopsis: An interactive chat-robot designed to engage with commuters in Singapore University of Tech and Design, using motors to move towards recognised humans and chat with them.
description:
Whiskers is an interactive mobile chat-robot designed to engage with commuters in Singapore University of Tech and Design, using motors to move towards recognised humans and chat with them. Whiskers seeks out visitors through facial recognition, conversing with them through a speaker and indicating emotions using lights.

This project was ideated and developed using the double diamond framework, and aims to use lights and sensors to increase social interactions in a less active area of the school.
process:
This project was made using the double diamond framework, as our team went through multiple rounds of research, ideation and site studies to identify the key problems and potential solutions to increase social interactivity at our chosen site. Once we settled on Whiskers as our solution, I worked on creating the movement logic and facial recognition on the Raspberry Pi 4.

For the proof-of-concept at our final presentation, we used a keyboard to control the robot movement, showcasing the proposed pathing of the robot.

name: Icarus
synopsis: Showcased during SUTD Open House 2024 and 2025. A bullet-hell inspired action arcade game, based on the Greek myth of Icarus, made using Godot for the SUTD Dev & Dice Arcade Machine.
description:
Icarus is a bullet-hell inspired action arcade game, based on the Greek myth of Icarus, made using Godot for the SUTD Dev & Dice Arcade Machine. The goal of the game is to survive for as long as you can, avoiding the wrath of Zeus, or the birds who share your path, while keeping your wings away from the waters or the clouds.

This game was showcased during SUTD Open House 2024 and 2025.
process:
This game was my first venture in Godot game development, as a solo project for the arcade machine controls. With this game, I aimed to create a competitive and engaging game with short gameplay potential that could be enjoyed by anyone who visited the club booth at the open house. I also sought to create a completely polished project, to limit test the capabilities of the engine, and so took the time to learnt shader logic in the engine.

I created all the art assets using Aseprite, and sourced for sounds on Freesound. I also refered extensively to Godot documentation to create the different systems within the game.
